title: Contact
metaTitle: Contact Us About Your Pennsylvania Mineral Rights
metaDescription: Reach out with questions about your Pennsylvania mineral or royalty interest. No pressure, no obligation, just honest answers before you decide anything.
heroLead: You don't need a finished plan to reach out. Most families who contact us are still figuring out what they even own.
intro: We hear from people at every stage of this process, someone who just inherited a fractional interest and doesn't know where to start, a family comparing an unsolicited letter against what their royalty statements actually show, an owner who's simply tired of the paperwork and wants to talk through options. Wherever you're starting from, that's a fine place to reach out from.
This page is for questions as much as it is for offers. If you're not ready to talk numbers yet and just want to understand your situation better, that's a conversation we're glad to have too.

sections.heading: What we can help with right away
paragraphs: If you're holding a royalty statement you don't understand, an unsolicited offer letter that feels off, or a division order you're unsure about signing, we can talk through what you're looking at, even if you never end up selling to us. We'd rather be a resource than a pressure tactic.
If you already know you want an evaluation, mention your county and whether your minerals are leased, unleased, or producing, and we can get moving faster on what we'll need from you.

sections.heading: What we'll ask you, and why
paragraphs: Expect us to ask about your county, your acreage if you know it, and whether there's a current lease or active well. We're not trying to pry, we're trying to give you an answer grounded in your actual situation rather than a generic one. If you don't have everything memorized, that's completely normal; we can help you figure out where to find what's missing.

We'll never ask for financial account information or a payment over the phone as part of an initial conversation. If anything about an interaction feels off, trust that instinct and ask questions before proceeding.

sections.heading: No pressure, no deadline
paragraphs: Reaching out doesn't start a clock. Take whatever time you need to gather documents, talk with family members who share the interest, or get a second opinion from an attorney or another buyer. We'd genuinely rather answer the same question twice than have you sign something you're not confident about.

If your family situation is complicated, split ownership, an estate that never went through probate, a deed still in a relative's name, tell us that upfront. We've worked through similar situations before and can tell you honestly what it takes to sort out.

sections.heading: The best ways to reach us
paragraphs: Use the contact form on this page, call the number listed, or send an email, whichever is easiest for you. If you're reaching out about an urgent deadline on someone else's offer letter, mention that upfront so we can prioritize getting back to you quickly.
If you'd rather write everything out first, that works too. Some families find it easier to explain their situation in an email before getting on the phone, and we're glad to start that way.

sections.heading: What happens after you reach out
paragraphs: We'll follow up to ask a few clarifying questions about your county and your interest, then let you know what documents would help us give you a grounded answer. From there, the pace is largely up to you; some families move quickly, others take weeks or months to gather everything and decide what they want to do.

faqs.question: Do I have to know exactly what I own before contacting you?
faqs.answer: No. Many people who reach out are still figuring that out, and we can help point you toward your county recorder of deeds or register of wills if you need to track something down.

faqs.question: Can I ask questions without getting a sales pitch?
faqs.answer: Yes. We're glad to explain a royalty statement, a division order, or an unsolicited letter you've received, even if it doesn't lead to a sale with us.

faqs.question: What information should I have ready when I reach out?
faqs.answer: Your county, roughly how many acres you believe you own, and whether your minerals are leased, unleased, or producing is a good starting point. Your deed and statements can come later.

faqs.question: Is there any cost or obligation to contacting you?
faqs.answer: No. There's no cost to reach out, and no obligation to move forward with an offer once you've heard it.

faqs.question: What if several family members need to be involved?
faqs.answer: That's fine, and common. Let us know upfront if the interest is shared among heirs, and we can walk through the process in a way that works for the whole family.

faqs.question: How quickly will someone get back to me?
faqs.answer: We typically respond quickly to a first message. If your inquiry mentions a deadline on someone else's offer, say so and we'll try to prioritize accordingly.

faqs.question: Can I reach out on behalf of an elderly parent or relative?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's common. Let us know your relationship and, if you have any authority to act for them, like a power of attorney, mention that too so we can move forward correctly.
